questions.q: Which event overrides the other failsafes?
questions.explain: Critical battery — usually Land from any state.
1 RTL, 3 SmartRTL/RTL, 4 SmartRTL/Land, 5 Land, 6 DO_LAND_START/RTL, 7 Brake/Land.

questions.q: What do you need to configure in the receiver for the RC failsafe to work correctly?
options: No pulses or throttle below FS_THR_VALUE
questions.explain: Otherwise the firmware won't find out that the link is lost.

options: The altitude at which landing starts
The home point altitude above sea level
questions.explain: The minimum altitude above home for the return; if the vehicle is higher, it returns at its current altitude. It must be above the obstacles at the field.

questions.q: What is RPN in an FMEA?
options: The battery failsafe threshold in percent
questions.explain: Mitigations are prioritized by descending RPN.

options: Landing in any case regardless of the mode
questions.explain: For authorized BVLOS; without an authorization, keep it off.

questions.q: What should you verify in SITL before going to the field?
options: Only RC loss and only in Loiter
questions.explain: RC, GCS, battery, EKF, geofence, motor failure. Record: trigger, reaction, time, log.

questions.q: Pre-flight parameter audit. What is dangerous here?
options: No reaction to either RC loss or low voltage: FS_THR_ENABLE = 0 and BATT_FS_LOW_ACT = 0
FENCE_ENABLE = 1 without an uploaded polygon blocks arming and sends the vehicle into RTL
BATT_LOW_VOLT 14.0 is too high for 4S — the failsafe will trigger right after takeoff
FS_GCS_ENABLE = 0 forbids flying without a connected ground station — the vehicle simply won't arm
questions.explain: The voltage threshold is set, but the action is 0 — nothing will happen; the RC failsafe is off.
